# Context Window Management

Covers auto-compaction, manual compaction, /context visualization, token budgeting, and subagent context isolation.

## Context Window Size

Claude Code operates with a 200K token context window by default, expandable to 1M for Max, Team, and Enterprise users automatically [18][34]. 1M context became generally available for Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6 in March 2026 [18]. Standard model pricing applies — no premium beyond 200K tokens [18].

## What Consumes Context

The context window visualization at startup shows these components loading in order [6]:

| Component | Approximate Tokens | Notes |
|-----------|-------------------|-------|
| System prompt | ~4,200 | Core instructions, always loaded first |
| Auto memory (MEMORY.md) | ~680 | First 200 lines or 25KB |
| Environment info | ~280 | Working directory, platform, shell, OS, git state |
| MCP tools (deferred) | ~120 | Tool names only by default (schemas loaded on demand) |
| CLAUDE.md files | Varies | All discovered files loaded |
| Skills (descriptions) | Varies | Full content loads only when invoked |
| Messages + tool results | Grows over session | Primary context consumer |

## Auto-Compaction

Auto-compaction triggers when the context window approaches capacity [12]. The `CLAUDE_AUTOCOMPACT_PCT_OVERRIDE` environment variable controls the trigger threshold (1-100, default approximately 95%) [3]. The process:

1. Clears older tool outputs first [12]
2. Summarizes conversation if needed [12]
3. Preserves requests and key code snippets [12]
4. CLAUDE.md re-read from disk after compaction [8]
5. Nested CLAUDE.md not re-injected automatically (reloads on next file read) [8]

If a single file or tool output is so large that context refills immediately after each summary, Claude Code stops auto-compacting after a few attempts and shows an error [12].

## Manual Compaction (/compact)

`/compact [instructions]` compresses conversation history into a summary [17]. Optional steering instructions guide what to preserve:

```
/compact focus on the API changes
/compact keep only function names and current errors
```

The decision table for when to compact [17]:

| Situation | Tool | Rationale |
|-----------|------|-----------|
| Same task, relevant context | Continue | Everything still matters |
| Wrong approach taken | /rewind | Keep useful reads, drop failed attempt |
| Bloated session with stale content | /compact | Low effort, model determines relevance |
| New task starting | /clear | Zero rot, you define what's essential |

## /context Command

`/context` visualizes current context window usage with component-by-component breakdown [6]. Shows what's using space and provides optimization suggestions [6]. Run `/mcp` to check per-server MCP costs [12].

## Context Rot

Performance degrades as context grows — older, irrelevant content distracts from current task [17]. Proactive compaction before auto-compact triggers is recommended: "With one million context, you have more time to /compact proactively with a description of what you want to do" [17].

## What Survives Compaction

- Project-root CLAUDE.md: re-read from disk and re-injected [8]
- Nested CLAUDE.md: NOT re-injected, reloads on next file read in that subdirectory [8]
- Invoked skills: re-attached after summary, first 5,000 tokens each, combined 25,000 token budget [13]
- "Compact Instructions" section in CLAUDE.md: guides preservation [12]

## Subagent Context Isolation

Each subagent runs in its own context window with independent system prompt and tool access [9]. Intermediate tool calls and results stay inside the subagent — only the final summary returns to the parent conversation [9][17].

Use subagents when the intermediate work (searches, logs, file reads) would bloat the main context [17]. The subagent does extensive work, then synthesizes results so only the conclusion returns [17].

## Prompt Caching

Claude Code uses prompt caching to reduce costs and latency [36]. The cache TTL is 5 minutes [36]. Cache_control parameters mark reusable content boundaries [36]. Cost reduction up to 90% for repetitive tasks [36].

## MCP Tool Search

Tool search defers full MCP tool definitions until needed [6][24]:
- Only tool names load at session start (~120 tokens vs potentially 66,000+ for full definitions) [6][28]
- Activates automatically when MCP tools would consume >10% of context [27][28]
- Returns 3-5 most relevant tool_reference blocks when Claude needs a specific tool [24]
- Requires Sonnet 4+/Opus 4+ for tool_reference support [24]
- Configuration: `ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH` environment variable (auto, true, false) [27]
- Accuracy improvements documented: Opus 4 49% to 74%, Opus 4.5 79.5% to 88.1% on MCP evaluations [23]

## Gaps and Limitations

- Exact auto-compaction trigger threshold varies by source (95%, 98%, or "approximately 95%") — the official env var default is approximately 95% [3]
- No official documentation quantifies information loss during compaction
- Platform-specific thresholds (VS Code extension vs CLI) reported by community sources but not confirmed in official docs [discovery agent findings]
- Quality degradation at approximately 67% capacity reported by community but not in official docs [discovery agent findings]
